edges.mechanism: Concomitant MAOI use or use within 14 days of stopping (including linezolid, IV methylene blue) can cause hypertensive crisis with stroke, MI, aortic dissection or death.
edges.evidence: FDA label contraindication

edges.with: serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, tramadol, fentanyl, buspirone, tryptophan, St John's wort)
edges.mechanism: Additive serotonergic activity; label warns of potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome. Start at lower dose and monitor; stop both if symptoms occur.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning; case report of serotonin toxicity with therapeutic dexamphetamine plus venlafaxine

edges.with: CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine, bupropion, quinidine, ritonavir)
edges.mechanism: Amphetamine is partly CYP2D6-metabolized; inhibitors may raise exposure (equivalent to a dose increase) and serotonin-syndrome risk. Bupropion included as a CYP2D6 inhibitor by class inference.
edges.evidence: FDA label; DDI review; no dedicated dextroamphetamine PK study found

edges.mechanism: Striking and sustained increases in brain d-amphetamine and potentiated cardiovascular effects; TCAs are also serotonergic.
edges.evidence: FDA label

edges.with: alkalinizing agents (sodium bicarbonate, acetazolamide, some thiazides)
edges.mechanism: Urinary/GI alkalinization reduces ionized fraction and renal elimination, raising amphetamine levels and effects; label says avoid GI alkalinizers.
edges.evidence: FDA label; human PK study of urinary pH effect

edges.with: acidifying agents (ascorbic acid, ammonium chloride, methenamine, glutamic acid HCl)
edges.mechanism: Urinary/GI acidification increases amphetamine excretion and lowers levels and efficacy.
edges.evidence: FDA label; human PK study

edges.mechanism: Ascorbic acid is listed in the label as a GI acidifying agent that lowers amphetamine blood levels/efficacy; however 4 g/day ascorbic acid lowered urine pH by only 0.58 (non-significant) in one RCT, so effect at typical supplement doses is uncertain.
edges.evidence: Label statement plus indirect urine-pH RCT; no direct dextroamphetamine-vitamin C PK study

edges.mechanism: Reduced gastric acidity: omeprazole did not change total amphetamine exposure but shortened Tmax of mixed amphetamine salts XR (5 h to 2.75 h); label advises monitoring clinical effect.
edges.evidence: Crossover PK RCT (n=24, MAS XR/lisdexamfetamine) and label

edges.mechanism: Amphetamines may antagonize hypotensive effects and inhibit adrenergic blockers; daily amphetamine raises SBP ~1.9 mmHg and HR ~3.7 bpm.
edges.evidence: Label; Cochrane review of 56 RCTs (high certainty for BP rise)

edges.mechanism: Lithium may inhibit stimulant effects (label) and attenuated d-amphetamine euphoria/activation by ~60% and the SBP rise in small human studies; lithium is also listed among serotonergic drugs raising serotonin-syndrome risk.
edges.evidence: Label; small controlled human studies (n=8-9)

edges.mechanism: Additive sympathomimetic effects: 300 mg caffeine and 20 mg d-amphetamine each raised DBP/HR in humans; caffeine potentiated amphetamine seizures and lethality in rats.
edges.evidence: Human single-dose comparison (not co-administration) and animal toxicity data; no controlled human combination study

edges.mechanism: Mechanistic inference: catecholamine-precursor depletion reduced amphetamine-induced striatal dopamine release and subjective effects, implying precursor availability modulates response; effect of tyrosine supplementation untested.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic human depletion studies only (PET n=8; RCT n=15)

edges.mechanism: Alcohol may increase plasma dextroamphetamine; dextroamphetamine masks ethanol psychomotor impairment without reducing perceived intoxication; FDA advises not combining stimulants with alcohol.
edges.evidence: DDI review; small crossover RCT (n=12); FDA communication

edges.mechanism: Sudden death reported in structural cardiac abnormalities; BP/HR increases; long-term use associated with CVD (AOR 1.04 per year), especially hypertension.
edges.evidence: Label warning; Cochrane MA; Swedish case-control

edges.mechanism: May exacerbate psychosis or induce mania; prescription amphetamine associated with incident psychosis/mania (AOR 2.68; 5.28-fold at >30 mg/day) and higher risk than methylphenidate.
edges.evidence: Label; case-control; claims cohort; 2025 MA

edges.mechanism: High abuse/misuse/addiction potential (boxed warning); 9.0% of adults using prescription stimulants had use disorder, more with amphetamines.
edges.evidence: FDA boxed warning; NSDUH analysis

edges.mechanism: No malformation signal for amphetamines in first trimester, but continuation into later pregnancy associated with pre-eclampsia, placental abruption and preterm birth; label advises use only if benefit justifies risk.
edges.evidence: Large cohort studies; label

edges.mechanism: Amphetamines are excreted in human milk; label advises refraining from nursing.
edges.evidence: FDA label

edges.mechanism: Stimulants may lower the convulsive threshold; discontinue if seizures occur.
edges.evidence: Label; RCT data only for methylphenidate

edges.mechanism: Stimulants associated with onset or worsening of tics; high-dose dextroamphetamine worsened tics in one short trial.
edges.evidence: Label; Cochrane review (very low quality for dextroamphetamine)

edges.mechanism: Stimulant-associated peripheral vasculopathy; usually mild and reversible, rarely ulceration or amputation.
edges.evidence: Label; systematic review of 61 cases

edges.mechanism: Amphetamines can significantly elevate plasma corticosteroid levels (greatest in the evening) and may interfere with urinary steroid determinations.
edges.evidence: FDA label

edges.mechanism: Dextroamphetamine produces true-positive amphetamine screens; many other drugs cross-react (3.9-9.9% of positive screens are false positives), so confirm by GC-MS/LC-MS/MS.
edges.evidence: Laboratory reviews and 6-year lab audit

edges.mechanism: Reduced CYP2D6 metabolism; genotype-predicted poor metabolizers reported more symptom improvement (OR 3.67) without more side effects in youth; toxicology review notes poor or ultrarapid metabolizers may face toxicity.
edges.evidence: Single cross-sectional genotype study (n=214) and review; no dosing guideline
